content: 1. Wessberg A, Lundgren I, Elden H conducted a mixed-methods study on women's experiences of labor induction, published in Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand in 2013. The study explored the multifaceted experiences of women undergoing labor induction, providing insights into their emotional and physical responses. 2. Wessberg A, Lundgren I, Elden H also performed a phenomenological study on the lived experiences of women at 41 weeks of gestation and beyond, published in BMC Pregnancy Childbirth in 2017. This research highlighted the uncertainty and emotional challenges women face during prolonged pregnancies. 3. Westfall RE and Benoit C examined the rhetoric surrounding natural childbirth and its implications for women experiencing prolonged pregnancies and labor induction. Their findings, published in Social Science & Medicine in 2004, provided a critical perspective on societal and individual expectations. 4. Nippita TA, Porter M, Seeho SK, Morris JM, and Roberts CL conducted a qualitative study on variations in clinical decision-making for labor induction, published in BMC Pregnancy Childbirth in 2017. The study identified factors influencing healthcare providers' decisions and the variability in practice. 5. Ten Eikelder M, van Baaren GJ, Oude Rengerink K, Jozwiak M, de Leeuw JW, Kleiverda G, et al. compared the cost-effectiveness of labor induction using oral misoprostol versus a Foley catheter in a multicenter randomized controlled non-inferiority trial. Their findings were published in BJOG in 2018. 6. Ten Eikelder ML, Rengerink KO, Jozwiak M, De Leeuw JW, De Graaf IM, Van Pampus MG, et al. conducted the PROBAAT-II trial, a multicenter randomized controlled non-inferiority trial comparing oral misoprostol and Foley catheter for labor induction at term. The results were published in The Lancet in 2016. 7. Van Baaren GJ, Jozwiak M, Opmeer BC, Oude Rengerink K, Benthem M, Dijkstra MGK, et al. evaluated the cost-effectiveness of labor induction at term using a Foley catheter compared to vaginal prostaglandin E2 gel in the PROBAAT trial. Their findings were published in BJOG in 2013. 8. Jozwiak M, Rengerink KO, Benthem M, van Beek E, Dijkstra MG, De Graaf IM, et al. conducted an open-label randomized controlled trial comparing Foley catheter and vaginal prostaglandin E2 gel for labor induction at term (PROBAAT trial). The study was published in The Lancet in 2011. 9. The WHO report titled State of Inequality: Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health provides a comprehensive analysis of disparities in healthcare access and outcomes globally. 10. The 2019 WHO Global Monitoring Report on Primary Health Care highlights progress and challenges on the path to achieving universal health coverage. 11. Protheroe J, Brooks H, Chew-Graham C, Gardner C, and Rogers A conducted a qualitative study on patient participation across different socioeconomic backgrounds, published in the Journal of Health Psychology in 2013. The study explored barriers and facilitators to patient engagement in healthcare. 12. Tunçalp Ӧ, Were W, MacLennan C, Oladapo O, Gülmezoglu A, Bahl R, et al. outlined the WHO vision for improving the quality of care for pregnant women and newborns in a publication in BJOG in 2015. 13. Seijmonsbergen-Schemers AE, van den Akker T, Rydahl E, Beeckman K, Bogaerts A, Binfa L, et al. conducted a multinational cross-sectional study on variations in childbirth interventions across 13 high-income countries, published in PLoS Medicine in 2020. 14. Guerra GV, Cecatti JG, Souza JP, Faundes A, Morais SS, Gülmezoglu AM, et al. investigated factors and outcomes associated with labor induction in Latin America, with findings published in BJOG in 2009. 15. Vogel JP, Souza JP, and Gülmezoglu AM analyzed patterns and outcomes of labor induction in Africa and Asia using data from the WHO Global Survey on Maternal and Neonatal Health. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 16. Vogel JP, Gülmezoglu AMM, Hofmeyr GJ, and Temmerman M provided a global perspective on elective labor induction in a publication in Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2014. 17. The WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience emphasize evidence-based practices to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.
